hints: Focus on what type of reaction an aldehyde like ethanal undergoes with HCN, addition or substitution?
Notice that $\text{CN}^-$ is a good nucleophile that attacks the $\delta+$ carbon of the $\text{C=O}$ bond to give a negatively charged oxygen intermediate.
Consider how that $\text{O}^-$ intermediate becomes $\text{OH}$ and what molecule can supply the $\text{H}^+$ while regenerating the catalyst.
walkthrough:
**Name the reaction**

This is cyanohydrin formation. Ethanal undergoes nucleophilic addition, not substitution, because the $\text{C=O}$ double bond becomes a single bond with two new groups attached.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$$

**Attack by the real nucleophile**

$\text{KCN}$ provides $\text{CN}^-$. The carbon in $\text{CN}^-$ has a lone pair and attacks the $\delta+$ carbon of $\text{C=O}$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(CN)O}^-$$
This alkoxide ion is the key intermediate.

**Protonate the intermediate**

The $\text{O}^-$ needs an $\text{H}^+$ to become $\text{OH}$. Liquid $\text{HCN}$ acts as the proton donor.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(CN)O}^- + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(CN)OH} + \text{CN}^-$$
Notice $\text{CN}^-$ is reformed, so it is a catalyst.

**Choose the correct description**

Only the proton transfer from $\text{HCN}$ to the intermediate correctly describes the second step of this nucleophilic addition mechanism.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{HCN}$ ($\text{H-C}\equiv\text{N:}$) does have a lone pair on nitrogen. $\text{CN}^-$ is indeed the catalyst, but the reason given is false because both $\text{HCN}$ and $\text{CN}^-$ have lone pairs.
options.B: Incorrect. The nucleophile is $\text{CN}^-$, not $\text{O}^{\delta-}$, and the electrophile is the $\text{C}^{\delta+}$ of $\text{C=O}$, not $\text{K}^+$. $\text{K}^+$ is just a spectator ion.
options.C: Correct. After $\text{CN}^-$ adds to form $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(CN)O}^-$, $\text{HCN}$ donates $\text{H}^+$ to this intermediate to give the cyanohydrin $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$ and regenerate $\text{CN}^-$.
options.D: Incorrect. No atom or group is replaced. Both $\text{CN}$ and $\text{H}$ add across the $\text{C=O}$ double bond, so this is nucleophilic addition, not nucleophilic substitution.
